# FDG5096

> DO implement `operator <=` on types that implement `operator <` and `IEquatable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.7.3 Inequality Operators.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5096
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Define operator &lt;= on '{0}', which defines operator &lt; and implements IEquatable&lt;{0}>

FDG5096 reports an externally visible class or struct that declares operator &lt; and implements IEquatable&lt;T> with T the type itself, but declares no operator &lt;=. The report is on operator &lt;. Records implement IEquatable&lt;T> implicitly and are reported the same way. Adding an operator changes no existing signature, so the fix is not breaking, but there is no code fix.

## From the book

When both “less than” and “equal” are defined, then “less than or equal” should be well defined.
